citation: Bierman, K. L., Domitrovich, C. E., Nix, R. L., Gest, S. D., Welsh, J. A., Greenberg, M. T., Blair, C., Nelson, K. E., & Gill, S. (2008). Promoting Academic and Social-Emotional School Readiness: The Head Start REDI Program. Child Development, 79(6), 1802-1817. https://doi.org/10.1111/j.1467-8624.2008.01227.x
report_number: No IES/NCEE report number (peer-reviewed journal article, Child Development). NIH author manuscript NIHMSID NIHMS69218; PMCID PMC3549580; PMID 19037951.
design: Cluster-randomized RCT. 44 Head Start classrooms (in 3 Pennsylvania counties, 2 cohorts) randomly assigned to Head Start REDI enriched-intervention (n=22 classrooms) vs 'usual practice'/business-as-usual control (n=22 classrooms). Classrooms in the same Head Start center were always assigned to the same condition to avoid within-center contamination, so the effective unit of assignment is center/classroom (registry labels this 'School' level). Total N=356 four-year-old children (~178 per condition; 86% of eligible). REDI = manualized enrichment curricula (Preschool PATHS for social-emotional skills; interactive book-reading, Sound Games, alphabet-center activities for language/emergent literacy) plus 3-day summer training, a 1-day January booster, and weekly on-site mentoring/coaching from 'REDI trainers' (~3 hrs/classroom/week) -- i.e. TPD-for-curricula. Subjects = oral language, emergent literacy, and (excluded here) social-emotional/cognitive skills. Grade = Pre-K (Head Start, 4-year-olds). Outcomes measured at end of the one-year program (spring, March-April).
problems: (1) NO impact standard errors are reported anywhere. Table 3 reports, per outcome, raw pre/post group means with SDs and an HLM-based 'Intervention Effect' (approximate effect size, d) plus a p-value, but not the SE of the effect. p-values are given only to coarse precision (e.g. '.001', '.02', '.10', '.56', '.73'), so back-solving an SE from the p-value is unreliable (lower-bound for the '.001' rows, indeterminate for the large p rows). I therefore left impact_se null and computed a fallback design-based variance for each g (see g_method); these design-based variances are at the STUDENT level and do NOT account for classroom clustering. (2) The reported 'Intervention Effect' IS the cluster-accounting estimate: it is the HLM intervention-status coefficient from a two-level model (children nested within classroom), pretest-adjusted (preintervention score as a Level-1 covariate) plus child sex/race (Level 1) and site/cohort/intervention status (Level 2), with all measures standardized to mean 0, SD 1 (p.11-12). So the POINT ESTIMATE g is pretest-adjusted and cluster-adjusted; cluster_adjusted=true. But my g_var/g_se are NOT cluster-adjusted (no model SE available), so the central team should re-derive variance using n_clusters and a clustering ICC. (3) NO design-effect/clustering ICC is reported. The only ICCs in the paper (.70, .74) are inter-rater reliability ICCs for observer ratings, NOT the intra-class correlation of the outcome -- do not use them; icc left null (not guessed). (4) Exact analytic n per group per measure is NOT reported; the paper states only Total N=356 across 44 classrooms split 22/22 by condition. n_t=n_c=178 and n_clusters=22 per arm are the design split (even classroom distribution); per-measure analytic Ns will be somewhat lower due to missingness. (5) Table 3's parenthetical SDs are the RAW pre/post observed-score SDs, NOT the standardizing SD of the reported effect; because the model standardized every measure to SD=1, the 'Intervention Effect' is already a standardized (d-metric) coefficient and was NOT divided by the Table-3 raw SDs. (6) Six achievement contrasts extracted (all standardized published instruments): 3 oral-language (Vocabulary, Grammatical Understanding, Sentence Imitation -> outcome_subject Other) and 3 emergent-literacy (Blending, Elision, Print Awareness -> Reading). EXCLUDED as non-academic social-emotional/cognitive outcomes (noted, not extracted): Emotion Identification (ACES, d=.21), Emotion Recognition (ERQ, d=.23), CST Competent/Aggressive/Inept social-problem-solving responses (d=.35/-.21/-.28) from Table 3; and all of Table 4's behavioral ratings (teacher/parent/observer-rated social competence, aggression, attention problems, learning engagement/task orientation, communication). These are emotional-understanding / social-behavioral, not academic achievement.

effect_sizes.arm_label: Head Start REDI enriched intervention (manualized curricula + teacher training/mentoring) vs usual-practice Head Start (business-as-usual)
effect_sizes.test_name: Blending subtest, Test of Preschool Early Literacy (TOPEL; formerly Pre-CTOPP) -- phonological processing
effect_sizes.timepoint: post: end of the one-year Head Start program (spring, March-April)
effect_sizes.g_method: Reported HLM 'Intervention Effect' (approximate effect size) d=.39 (Table 3, p.23), standardized because all measures were rescaled to mean 0/SD 1 in the model (p.11-12); pretest-adjusted and cluster-accounted (children nested in classroom). Hedges g = J*d with df = n_t+n_c-2 = 354, J = 1 - 3/(4*354-1) = 0.997880, g = 0.997880*0.39 = 0.38917. Variance is a FALLBACK design-based estimate at the student level (no model SE reported): Var(d) = (n_t+n_c)/(n_t*n_c) + d^2/(2*(n_t+n_c)) = 356/31684 + 0.39^2/712 = 0.011425, Var(g)=J^2*Var(d)=0.011401, g_se=0.10678. NOT cluster-adjusted (see problems); central team should correct with n_clusters and an ICC (no ICC reported).
effect_sizes.page_ref: Table 3 (p.23 of PDF / journal p.1815); HLM/effect-size definition pp.11-12 (PDF) / pp.1809-1810
effect_sizes.notes: Emergent-literacy (phonological awareness) -> Reading. One of the strongest, statistically significant effects (d=.39, p=.001). Means/SDs shown are raw post-test observed scores (control 13.04/4.30; intervention 14.71/4.33); they are NOT the standardizing SD of the effect (effect is from the SD=1 standardized HLM). TOPEL is a published/standardized instrument (alpha=.86).
